public_rationale: The June 23, 2025 court order establishes that Anthropic used copyrighted books for training and found the training copies at issue were fair use [e1]. It separately found that downloading pirated copies to build a central library was not justified by fair use [e1]. These findings support the copyrighted-book training component, but do not establish training on “practically anything publicly available” [e1]. The order does not identify Marcus's books as acquired or used for training, so it cannot settle his personal allegation [e1].
limitations: The packet contains no independent title-level evidence connecting Marcus's books to Anthropic's acquisition or training.
The settlement lookup returned no usable records. This does not establish that his books were absent.
Acquisition does not by itself establish training use.
The training fair-use finding does not establish that acquisition was authorized.
The ethical judgment is not separately assessed.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Like OpenAI, Anthropic trained on practically anything publicly available, whether public domain or not, including some of Marcus's books, which hardly seems ethical.

statement.excerpt: Anthropic? Same thing. (Disclaimer, they ripped off some of my books, along the way.) Hardly seems ethical.
statement.document_title: There are no heroes in commercial AI

from_speaker: they ripped off some of my books
our_interpretation: “Same thing” incorporates the preceding claim of broad training on publicly accessible material including copyrighted works.
The personal allegation requires evidence connecting Marcus's books to Anthropic's acquisition and training practices.
“Ripped off” is read as unauthorized copying or use, without assuming every training use was legally infringing.
The ethical judgment is not separately scored and is not a condition that must occur.
The historical period ends at the post; no starting date is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: Records establish broad copyrighted-material training and identify Marcus-authored books copied or used as alleged, with evidence distinguishing acquisition from actual training.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records refute the broad copyrighted-training allegation or establish that the specifically alleged Marcus works were not copied or used.
